paragraphs: Here's what I want you to hold onto, friend. Pilate knew it was out of envy that Jesus was handed over to him (Matthew 27:18), and his wife called Him an "innocent man" (Matthew 27:19). Pilate himself asked, "What evil has He done?" (Matthew 27:23), and the crowd only shouted all the louder.

So why did it still end the way it did? Because knowing the truth and standing on it are two different things. Pilate saw a riot starting, took water, and tried to wash it all off his hands (Matthew 27:24). I'm telling you, friend, I've blamed a flat batch on the oven, the weather AND the flour, so I know that move, but water doesn't clean what's on your conscience.

And look at Jesus in the middle of all that noise. He gave no answer, not even to a single charge, much to the governor's amazement (Matthew 27:14). This story is not finished, friend, and we are not done being amazed. When the crowd gets loud, the truth doesn't get any smaller, so ask yourself where you'll stand.
